The test image shows a tomato plant pulled from soil, laid flat for examination. Key features:
- Entire plant wilted/collapsed
- Main stems show prominent pale/bleached, cream-white discoloration along their length
- Some darker brown lesion spots on stem
- Roots visible and tan/brown
- Leaves wilted, some browning

This looks like a vascular wilt disease with stem involvement. Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Southern_Blight, Bacterial_Wilt. Let me check one reference from each.
I've used 7 reference views. One more needed. The test image's Bugwood number (1568040) is close to Southern_Blight 1568116. Let me check one more reference for Bacterial_Canker stem symptoms.

**Analysis summary:**

Test image: Tomato plants pulled from soil, laid on a dark surface. Key features:
- Entire stems show prominent pale/cream/white bleaching throughout
- Brown lesion areas on stems
- Complete plant collapse/wilt
- Roots visible (tan/brown)
- Black plastic mulch context visible in background

Reference comparisons:
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Doesn't match — shows leaf yellowing pattern, different plant type
- **Bacterial_Canker Bugwood_1**: Leaf marginal scorch, no stem bleaching
- **Bacterial_Canker Bugwood_18**: Shows external stem canker/bleaching (right panel is somewhat similar, but localized)
- **Bacterial_Wilt Bugwood_3**: Streaming test image, no visual match
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot Bugwood_2**: Wilted branches on staked plant, no stem bleaching match
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt Bugwood_1**: Streaming test, no match
- **Southern_Blight Bugwood_5 & 13**: Similar field context (black plastic mulch), collapsed plants — BugwoodID 1568116 is adjacent to test image's 1568040
- **Bacterial_Canker Bugwood_18**: Partial stem bleaching on right panel, partial similarity

The pale/cream bleached stems with rapid whole-plant collapse on a black-mulch background best aligns with **Southern_Blight** (Athelia rolfsii), which causes water-soaking and bleaching of the cortex/stem tissue with rapid plant death.
